claim: Dynamic CpG methylation 'barcodes' were read from 15,000–21,000 single cells from three human male brains.
source: Dynamic CpG methylation 'barcodes' were read from 15,000–21,000 single cells from three human male brains.
evidence: The abstract directly states the number of cells analyzed from three brains, which is supported by the data presented in Table 1 showing 21,836, 16,161, and 15,434 cells for H01, H02, and H04 respectively.

claim: The barcode had ~31,000 rapidly fluctuating X-chromosome CpG sites (fCpGs).
source: To overcome sparse sequencing coverage, the barcode had ~31,000 rapidly fluctuating X-chromosome CpG sites (fCpGs), with at least 500 covered sites per cell and at least 30 common sites between cell pairs (average of ~48).
evidence: The manuscript describes the filtering process that resulted in ~31,000 fCpG sites used for analysis, with specific coverage criteria per cell.

claim: Barcodes appear to start methylated and record mitotic ages because excitatory neurons and glial cells that emerge later in development were less methylated.
source: Barcodes appear to start methylated and record mitotic ages because excitatory neurons and glial cells that emerge later in development were less methylated.
evidence: This claim is supported by the data shown in Figure 2A and 2B, which demonstrate higher methylation in early-appearing neurons (PN, THM) and lower methylation in later-appearing excitatory neurons and glial cells.

claim: Average pairwise differences (PWDs) between cells were ~0.5.
source: Barcodes are different between most cells, with average pairwise differences (PWDs) of ~0.5 between cells.
evidence: Table 1 shows average PWD values of 0.47 for all three brains, and Figure 1B displays the distribution of PWDs centered around 0.5.

claim: About 10 cell pairs per million were more closely related with PWDs <0.05.
source: About 10 cell pairs per million were more closely related with PWDs <0.05.
evidence: Table 1 shows closely related pairs per million ranging from 7.0 to 14.8, with an average around 10 per million.

claim: Inhibitory neurons showed more evidence of tangential migration than excitatory neurons, with related cells in different cortical regions.
source: Inhibitory neurons showed more evidence of tangential migration than excitatory neurons, with related cells in different cortical regions.
evidence: Figure 5C and 5D show that nearest neighbor inhibitory neuron pairs were found in the same cortical region ~25% of the time, while excitatory neurons were co-localized ~50% of the time, indicating more tangential migration for inhibitory neurons.

claim: fCpG barcodes become polymorphic during development and can distinguish between thousands of human cells.
source: fCpG barcodes become polymorphic during development and can distinguish between thousands of human cells.
evidence: The manuscript demonstrates that barcodes from 15,000-21,000 cells show sufficient polymorphism with average PWDs of ~0.47, indicating most cells have unique barcodes.

claim: DNA methylation replication errors are much higher compared to base replication.
source: DNA methylation patterns are usually copied between cell divisions, but replication errors are much higher compared to base replication, allowing for more differences between daughter cells.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about DNA methylation replication error rates.

claim: Most fCpG sites are present outside of genes or in unexpressed genes.
source: DNA methylation modulates expression and their patterns can be used to infer cell phenotypes (Tian et al., 2023; Loyfer et al., 2023), but most fCpG sites are present outside of genes or in unexpressed genes.
evidence: Supplementary file 1 indicates that 16% of fCpG sites are within genes or promoters, implying 84% are outside genes.

claim: Brain growth is largely prenatal.
source: Although billions of cells are present in an adult brain, lineage trees are compact because growth is largely prenatal.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about brain development.

claim: Brain development roughly follows a caudal to rostral pattern.
source: The brain also allows for serial 'stopwatch' barcode sampling because development roughly follows a caudal to rostral pattern, and groups of neurons characteristically stop dividing and differentiate at different times and locations (Stiles and Jernigan, 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Stiles and Jernigan, 2010, and is consistent with established developmental biology.

claim: Brainstem neurons emerge early during development.
source: Brainstem neurons emerge early (Fan et al., 2020) and their barcodes should most resemble the initial progenitor state, whereas the stopwatch runs longer for excitatory neurons that appear later in development.
evidence: This is supported by citation to Fan et al., 2020, and is consistent with the barcode methylation data showing higher methylation in brainstem neurons.

claim: The brain fCpG barcode initializes as predominately methylated in the progenitor cell.
source: The brain fCpG barcode initializes as predominately methylated in the progenitor cell and becomes polymorphic with more diverse barcodes in excitatory neurons that emerge later in development.
evidence: Figure 2B shows that nearly all individual fCpGs are methylated in early-appearing inhibitory neurons in the subcortex (PN, THM, MSN), supporting the inference of a methylated starting state.

claim: Single-cell methylation data has sparse coverage with <5% of CpG sites sequenced.
source: Barcode development was limited by the sparse single-cell data (Tian et al., 2023), with <5% of CpG sites sequenced, often with only a single read.
evidence: This describes a technical limitation of the data source used in the study.

claim: X-chromosome fCpG sites require only a single read to infer a binary state in male individuals.
source: Sparse coverage was mitigated with X-chromosome fCpG sites because only a single read can infer a binary (0, 1) state in male individuals.
evidence: This is based on the biological knowledge that males have only one X chromosome, so methylation state is binary rather than requiring multiple reads to determine heterozygosity.

claim: Autosomal CpG sites require at least 2 reads to infer three possible states (0, 0.5, 1).
source: Autosomal CpG sites require at least 2 reads to infer three possible states (0, 0.5, 1).
evidence: This is based on the biological knowledge that autosomal chromosomes are diploid, requiring assessment of both alleles.

claim: CpG sites with average methylation between 0.25 and 0.75 in bulk neurons are likely polymorphic.
source: The X-chromosome also simplifies the identification of polymorphic fCpGs because many neurons have different binary states if average methylation is between 0.25 and 0.75 in bulk WGBS adult male neurons reference data (Loyfer et al., 2023).
evidence: This is an inference based on the logic that intermediate methylation levels in bulk samples indicate heterogeneity at the single-cell level.

claim: Approximately 116,000 CpG sites had average methylation between 0.25 and 0.75 in bulk neurons from seven males.
source: CpG sites (N ~116,000), with average methylation between 0.25 and 0.75 in bulk neurons from seven males (Loyfer et al., 2023), were further filtered by discarding more stable CpG sites with average methylation less than 0.2 or more than 0.8 for all cells, inhibitory neurons, and excitatory neurons in brain H02.
evidence: This describes the initial filtering step in the barcode development process using reference data.

claim: fCpG site methylation appears neutral because they are predominately intergenic.
source: fCpG site methylation appears neutral because they are predominately intergenic, with 16% within genes or promoters (Supplementary file 1).
evidence: The inference of neutrality is based on the observation that 84% of fCpG sites are outside genes or promoters, suggesting they are not under strong selection.

claim: Analyzed cells had at least 500 fCpGs with an average of ~1100.
source: Analyzed cells had at least 500 fCpGs (average ~1100), with pairwise distances (PWDs) calculated between cell pairs when at least 30 fCpGs were comparable (average ~48 fCpGs per cell pair).
evidence: Table 1 shows average fCpG per cell ranging from 1060 to 1170, consistent with the stated average of ~1100.

claim: Average fCpG methylation was ~58% for all three brains.
source: fCpG methylation was variable between cells with averages of ~58% for all three brains (Figure 1A).
evidence: Table 1 shows average methylation per cell of 0.58 for all three brains, and Figure 1A displays this distribution.

claim: Average methylation was highest in the pons (PN) and thalamus (THM).
source: Methylation was variable between cells of the same type and average methylation was highest in the pons (PN) and thalamus (THM), intermediate for other inhibitory neurons, and lowest for excitatory neurons, glial cells, and cerebellar cells (Figure 2A).
evidence: Figure 2A shows violin plots with PN and THM having the highest methylation levels among all cell types.

claim: Outer layer cortical excitatory neurons (L2_3) that are made later during development were less methylated than inner cortical excitatory neurons (L4_6) that appear earlier.
source: Outer layer cortical excitatory neurons (L2_3) that are made later during development were less methylated than inner cortical excitatory neurons (L4_6) that appear earlier.
evidence: Figure 2A shows L2_3 neurons with lower methylation than L4_6 neurons, consistent with the known developmental timeline where outer layers form after inner layers.

claim: Predominantly methylated individual fCpG sites were common in subcortical neurons (PN, THM), less frequent in other inhibitory neurons, and rare in excitatory neurons.
source: Predominantly methylated individual fCpG sites were common in subcortical neurons (PN, THM), less frequent in other inhibitory neurons, and rare in excitatory neurons (Figure 2B).
evidence: Figure 2B shows histograms of individual fCpG methylation states for different cell types, demonstrating this pattern.

claim: Barcodes become fixed when their cells stop dividing and differentiate.
source: Barcodes are assumed to become fixed when their cells stop dividing and differentiate.
evidence: This is a logical inference based on the mechanism of methylation changes occurring during DNA replication.

claim: The hindbrain with mature neurons forms early in development, followed by inhibitory neurons in the ganglionic eminences, and then excitatory neurons and glial cells in the cortex.
source: Very simplistically, the hindbrain with mature neurons (Fan et al., 2020) forms early in development, followed by inhibitory neurons in the ganglionic eminences, and then excitatory neurons and glial cells in the cortex.
evidence: This is supported by citation to Fan et al., 2020, and represents established knowledge of brain development.

claim: Average barcode PWDs were lowest in brainstem cells (PN), intermediate between other inhibitory neurons, and highest for excitatory neurons.
source: A progenitor cell barcode is assumed to become increasingly polymorphic with subsequent divisions. This pattern was observed, with average barcode PWDs lowest in brainstem cells (PN), intermediate between other inhibitory neurons, and highest for excitatory neurons (Figure 3A).
evidence: Figure 3A shows violin plots of PWDs for different cell types, demonstrating this pattern of increasing PWD with developmental time.

claim: Cells of the same phenotype were more similar with lower average PWDs.
source: Cells of the same phenotype were more similar with lower average PWDs (Figure 3A and B), suggesting they are more related to each other and have common progenitors.
evidence: Figure 3B shows a heatmap where cells of the same phenotype cluster together with lower PWDs.

claim: Closely related cell pairs were ~2.9 times more frequent within a brain compared to between brains.
source: Closely related cell pairs were ~2.9 times more frequent within a brain (average ~9.8 per million) compared to between brains (average ~3.4 per million).
evidence: Table 1 shows closely related pairs per million averaging 9.8 within brains (7.0, 7.5, 14.8) and 3.4 between brains (2.8, 3.7, 3.7), supporting this calculation.

claim: Closely related cells had fewer matching fCpG sites (~35 compared to ~48 for all cell pairs).
source: Closely related cells had fewer matching fCpG sites (~35 compared to ~48 for all cell pairs) and were more common early in development when barcodes are more methylated (Figure 3C), indicating that lower barcode complexity favors matching.
evidence: Table 1 shows fCpG per nearest neighbor pair averaging 34-35, while fCpG per pair for all comparisons averages 45-51.

claim: fCpG barcodes from ~1000 brain cells with different phenotypes yield trees that resemble caudal to rostral development.
source: fCpG barcodes from ~1000 brain cells with different phenotypes yield trees with a standard phylogeny software that resemble caudal to rostral development (Figure 4).
evidence: Figure 4 shows phylogenetic trees constructed from barcode data that show sequential branching consistent with known developmental patterns.

claim: The trees are rooted by a progenitor with a fully methylated barcode.
source: The trees are rooted by a progenitor with a fully methylated barcode, and branches progressively yield brainstem neurons (PN), a subset of excitatory lower (L4_6) neurons, thalamic neurons (THM), inhibitory neurons, cerebellar cells, and glial cells.
evidence: Figure 4 shows trees rooted at a fully methylated progenitor, which is an assumption used to orient the tree based on the inferred starting state.

claim: Hippocampal neurons (CA, DG) that may divide postnatally were at the terminus of the trees.
source: Excitatory neurons branch last, and hippocampal neurons (CA, DG) that may divide postnatally (Gage, 2002) were at the terminus.
evidence: Figure 4 shows hippocampal neurons at the end of the tree branches, consistent with citation to Gage, 2002, about postnatal neurogenesis.

claim: Bootstrap branch support in the trees was typically less than 15%.
source: The trees illustrate the ability to produce phylogenies with IQtree, but the phylogenies are limited by sparse cell sampling and that barcodes may be similar by chance. The degree of confidence was generally low, with bootstrap branch support typically less than 15%.
evidence: This is stated as a limitation of the phylogenetic analysis, indicating low statistical confidence in specific branch relationships.

claim: Inhibitory neurons have higher lineage fidelity (>90%) than excitatory neurons.
source: Lineage fidelity was high (>90%) for inhibitory neurons (Figure 5A). Excitatory lineage fidelity was slightly lower, indicating that some excitatory and inhibitory neurons may share common progenitors (Delgado et al., 2022).
evidence: Figure 5A shows that nearest neighbor pairs of inhibitory neurons were nearly always both inhibitory neurons, while excitatory neurons had more mixed nearest neighbors.

claim: The barcodes documented switching between inhibitory neuron subtypes.
source: The barcodes documented the known switching between inhibitory neuron subtypes (Figure 5B).
evidence: Figure 5B shows that nearest neighbor inhibitory neuron pairs often had subtype differences, indicating lineage relationships between different inhibitory subtypes.

claim: Nearest neighbor inhibitory cortical neuron pairs were found in the same cortical region ~25% of the time.
source: Nearest neighbor inhibitory cortical neuron pairs were found in the same cortical region ~25% of the time (Figure 5C and D).
evidence: Figure 5C and 5D show location fidelity data for nearest neighbor pairs, with inhibitory neurons showing lower same-region localization than excitatory neurons.

claim: Nearest neighbor excitatory neuron pairs were in the same cortical region ~50% of the time.
source: Nearest neighbor excitatory neuron pairs were also scattered throughout the cortex, but less than inhibitory neurons, and were in the same cortical region ~50% of the time.
evidence: Figure 5C and 5D show that excitatory neurons had approximately twice the location fidelity of inhibitory neurons.

claim: Greater localized excitatory neuron migration was seen when trees were reconstructed with more (~2800) neurons.
source: Greater localized excitatory neuron migration was seen when trees were reconstructed with more (~2800) neurons, while inhibitory neurons still showed scattered tangential migration (Figure 4D).
evidence: Figure 4D shows a tree with ~2853 cortical excitatory neurons demonstrating more evidence of localized radial migration.

claim: Related lower and upper excitatory neuron pairs were uncommon.
source: Hence, lineage trees appear to increase their resolution with more cells, albeit related lower and upper excitatory neuron pairs were still uncommon, which may reflect the unlikely chance of sampling very small radial clonal units.
evidence: This observation is based on the analysis of trees with more neurons, with the interpretation that sparse sampling limits detection of small clonal units.

claim: fCpG barcodes are potential markers of somatic cell ancestry and not cell type classifiers.
source: fCpG barcodes are potential markers of somatic cell ancestry and not cell type classifiers, although cells of the same phenotype are often related because they originate from common progenitors (see new Supplement for fuller discussion).
evidence: This is a conceptual distinction made by the authors about the purpose and interpretation of the barcode system.

claim: The brain periodically stores neurons that stop recording at relatively defined times and locations.
source: The brain facilitates barcode validation because it periodically stores neurons that stop recording at relatively defined times and locations (McKenna and Gagnon, 2019; Finlay and Darlington, 1995).
evidence: This is supported by citations to McKenna and Gagnon, 2019, and Finlay and Darlington, 1995, describing the developmental biology of the brain.

claim: Barcode methylation may indicate when different neurons that survive to adulthood appear in the neonatal brain.
source: Barcode methylation may indicate when different neurons that survive to adulthood appear in the neonatal brain (Figure 2C).
evidence: Figure 2C shows a correlation between barcode methylation levels and the developmental timeline of different neuron types, supporting this inference.

claim: Most inhibitory and excitatory neurons have relatively distinct progenitors.
source: The current barcode indicates that most inhibitory and excitatory neurons have relatively distinct progenitors, consistent with the lineage dendrograms reconstructed with neuron-specific methylation of the same data (Tian et al., 2023).
evidence: This is based on the high lineage fidelity observed in Figure 5A and is consistent with previous analysis of the same dataset.

claim: There was evidence for common inhibitory and excitatory progenitors, primarily for earlier emerging excitatory neurons.
source: There was also evidence for common inhibitory and excitatory progenitors (Delgado et al., 2022), primarily for earlier emerging excitatory neurons.
evidence: This is based on the observation that some excitatory neurons had inhibitory nearest neighbors, particularly earlier in development, as shown in the lineage trees.

claim: Tangential migration is seen with sequencing studies that find neurons with specific mutations in multiple brain regions.
source: Tangential migration is also seen with sequencing studies that find neurons with specific mutations in multiple brain regions (Lodato et al., 2015; Breuss et al., 2022; Chung et al., 2024; Evrony et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to studies that have documented tangential migration using somatic mutations as lineage markers.

claim: fCpGs more efficiently distinguish between cells than mutations due to higher replication error rates.
source: fCpGs more efficiently distinguish between cells than mutations due to higher replication error rates.
evidence: This is based on the known higher error rate of DNA methylation replication compared to base replication, allowing for more rapid accumulation of differences.

claim: Fully demethylated neurons were not observed.
source: Although average methylation decreases with time, both demethylation and remethylation are likely because fully demethylated neurons were not observed, and balanced fluctuating methylation is inferred in other tissues when CpG sites are ~50% methylated in bulk tissues (Gabbutt et al., 2022).
evidence: This observation is based on the data shown in Figure 1A and Figure 2A, where no neurons show complete demethylation.

claim: More adult divisions in brain cancers did not saturate the barcode with average fCpG methylation remaining ~50%.
source: More adult divisions in brain cancers did not saturate the barcode with average fCpG methylation ~50% (Figure 3—figure supplement 3).
evidence: Figure 3—figure supplement 3 shows brain tumor samples with average methylation around 50%, indicating the barcode does not become fully demethylated even with many additional divisions.

claim: Fluctuating methylation complicates lineage tracing but backmutations can be modeled for ancestral reconstructions.
source: Fluctuating methylation complicates lineage tracing but backmutations can be modeled for ancestral reconstructions.
evidence: This is a methodological consideration based on the use of the GTR2 model in IQtree that accounts for backmutation.

claim: Lineage resolution could be improved by combining mutations and fCpGs.
source: Lineage resolution could be improved by combining mutations and fCpGs.
evidence: This is a speculative suggestion for future methodological improvement.

claim: Interpretation of the barcodes relies on several untested assumptions, including relatively constant error rates between fCpG sites and through aging, neutrality, and a predominately fully methylated start in the progenitor cell.
source: Interpretation of the barcodes relies on several untested assumptions, including relatively constant error rates between fCpG sites and through aging, neutrality, and a predominately fully methylated start in the progenitor cell.
evidence: The authors explicitly acknowledge these assumptions as limitations of the study.

claim: Epigenetic remodeling occurs after progenitors stop dividing.
source: Epigenetic remodeling occurs after progenitors stop dividing (Ciceri et al., 2024), which could erase ancestral barcode information.
evidence: This is supported by citation to Ciceri et al., 2024, and represents a potential confounding factor.

claim: Neurons of the same type were both closely and remotely related, indicating that epigenetic remodeling does not systematically alter the fCpG sites.
source: However, neurons of the same type were both closely and remotely related, indicating that such epigenetic remodeling does not systematically alter the fCpG sites.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observation that cells of the same type show a range of PWDs, suggesting the barcode signal is preserved despite potential remodeling.

claim: A barcode of 100 fCpGs has enough complexity (2^100 or ~1 × 10^30) to potentially distinguish between most excitatory neurons.
source: A barcode of 100 fCpGs has enough complexity (2100 or ~1 × 1030) to potentially distinguish between most excitatory neurons, with less resolution early in development when cells are inherently more related.
evidence: This is a theoretical calculation based on the combinatorial complexity of binary states.

claim: Many polymorphisms linked to brain abnormalities such as autism are in neuronal proliferation, migration, and maturation pathways.
source: Many polymorphisms linked to brain abnormalities such as autism are in neuronal proliferation, migration, and maturation pathways (Pan et al., 2019), and this preliminary survey indicates lineage heterogeneity between individuals (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Pan et al., 2019, and the observation of differences in tree structure between individuals shown in Figure 4A.

claim: fCpG barcodes have been applied to the intestines, endometrium, and blood.
source: fCpG barcodes have been applied to the intestines, endometrium, and blood (Gabbutt et al., 2022), and could be found for multiple other tissue types, helping to unravel human development and aging.
evidence: This is supported by citation to Gabbutt et al., 2022, describing previous applications of the fCpG barcode approach.

claim: Single-cell files were downloaded from GEO (GSE215353) and supplemental files from Tian et al., 2023.
source: Single-cells with their annotations and methylation at each fCpG site were read from single-cell files downloaded from GEO (GSE215353) and supplemental files from reference (Tian et al., 2023).
evidence: This describes the data source used in the study.

claim: PWDs were calculated between all cell pairs with at least 30 matching fCpG sites.
source: PWDs were calculated between all cell pairs with at least 30 matching fCpG sites, with PWD data matrices in Supplementary file 6.
evidence: This describes the methodological criterion for pairwise comparisons.

claim: IQtree was run on a server with 64 cpus and 32 GB of memory.
source: IQtree (Nguyen et al., 2015) tree was downloaded and run on a server with 64 cpus and 32 GB of memory.
evidence: This describes the computational resources used for phylogenetic analysis.

claim: The model (GTR2 + FO + G4) accounts for backmutation and binary data with missing values.
source: The model (GTR2 + FO + G4) accounts for backmutation and binary data with missing values.
evidence: This describes the phylogenetic model used in IQtree analysis.

claim: Bootstraps were 1,000 per tree with 3000 iterations for whole brain (~1000 cells) trees and 1000 iterations for inhibitory or excitatory (~2,800 neurons) trees.
source: Bootstraps were 1,000 per tree with 3000 iterations for whole brain (~1000 cells) trees and 1000 iterations for inhibitory or excitatory (~2,800 neurons) trees.
evidence: This describes the bootstrap parameters used for assessing tree confidence.

claim: Epigenomes from 15,434–21,836 cells were downloaded from three male brains with a general criterion of allc.tsv.gz file sizes 90 mb or larger.
source: Epigenomes from 15,434–21,836 cells were downloaded from three male brains with a general criterion of allc.tsv.gz file sizes 90 mb or larger (Table 1).
evidence: This describes the data selection criterion based on file size as a proxy for data quality.

claim: Neurons were preferentially sampled, whereas glial cells were sometimes excluded.
source: Neurons were preferentially sampled, whereas glial cells were sometimes excluded (Supplementary file 2).
evidence: This describes a sampling bias in the dataset used.

claim: A PWD of 0 is a perfect match and 0.5 indicates randomization.
source: A PWD of 0 is a perfect match and 0.5 indicates randomization.
evidence: This defines the interpretation of the PWD metric used throughout the study.

claim: The 73–197 million possible cell pair comparisons revealed polymorphic barcodes with average PWDs of ~0.47 between cells.
source: The 73–197 million possible cell pair comparisons revealed polymorphic barcodes with average PWDs of ~0.47 between cells (Figure 1B).
evidence: Table 1 shows the number of cell pairs per million (73-197 million total) and average PWDs of 0.47 for all three brains.

claim: Barcodes for each cell type had a range of methylation, consistent with asynchronous development rather than a strict stepwise process.
source: Barcodes for each cell type had a range of methylation (Figure 2A), consistent with synchronous development rather than a strict stepwise process.
evidence: Figure 2A shows violin plots with wide distributions of methylation within each cell type, supporting the inference of asynchronous development.

claim: After barcodes change from ~100 to ~70% methylated, most adult brainstem (PN) and inhibitory neurons are present but excitatory neurons are fewer.
source: For example, after barcodes change from ~100 to~70% methylated, most adult brainstem (PN) and inhibitory neurons are present but excitatory neurons are fewer, with very few adult outer layer (L2_3) neurons.
evidence: This is an interpretation of Figure 2C, which shows the cumulative proportion of different cell types at different methylation levels.

claim: Outer excitatory and glial progenitor cells are present early but their barcodes continue to demethylate until they stop dividing and differentiate later in development.
source: Outer excitatory and glial progenitor cells are present (Eze et al., 2021), but their barcodes continue to demethylate until they stop dividing and differentiate later in development.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observation that outer layer neurons have lower methylation, combined with citation to Eze et al., 2021, about progenitor cell presence.

claim: This stopwatch-like pattern, with more demethylated barcodes in later appearing cell types, was present in all three adult brains.
source: This stopwatch-like pattern, with more demethylated barcodes in later appearing cell types, was present in all three adult brains.
evidence: Figure 2—figure supplements 1 and 2 show similar patterns for H02 and H04 as described for H01.

claim: Cells of the same phenotype are more related to each other and have common progenitors.
source: Cells of the same phenotype were more similar with lower average PWDs (Figure 3A and B), suggesting they are more related to each other and have common progenitors.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observation that same-phenotype cells have lower PWDs, which is consistent with shared ancestry.

claim: Lower barcode complexity favors matching by chance.
source: Closely related cells had fewer matching fCpG sites (~35 compared to ~48 for all cell pairs) and were more common early in development when barcodes are more methylated (Figure 3C), indicating that lower barcode complexity favors matching.
evidence: This is an inference that some closely related pairs may be false positives due to chance matching when barcode complexity is lower.

claim: Trees are similar between the brains, with H04 inferring less distance between inhibitory and excitatory lineages.
source: Similar trees were observed for H02 and H04, albeit with less separation between inhibitory and excitatory neurons for H04 (Figure 4A).
evidence: Figure 4A shows three trees with generally similar structure but some individual variation, particularly for H04.

claim: Cells are generally grouped by phenotype in the lineage trees.
source: Cells are generally grouped by phenotype, with some early appearing excitatory neurons admixed among inhibitory neurons.
evidence: Figure 4B shows that neurons of the same type tend to cluster together in the tree, with some exceptions.

claim: Most neurons sampled from the brainstem and hippocampal regions are related and localized to their respective regions.
source: Trees (Figure 4C) indicate that most neurons sampled from the brainstem and hippocampal regions are related and localized to their respective regions.
evidence: Figure 4C shows that neurons from these regions cluster together in the tree and are color-coded to the same locations.

claim: Inhibitory neurons were scattered throughout the cortex, consistent with their differentiation in the ganglionic eminences and subsequent tangential migration to the cortex.
source: Inhibitory neurons were scattered throughout the cortex, consistent with their differentiation in the ganglionic eminences and subsequent tangential migration to the cortex.
evidence: Figure 4C shows inhibitory neurons with related barcodes in different cortical regions, consistent with known developmental biology of inhibitory neuron migration.

claim: The extent of migration is uncertain due to sparse sampling and because barcodes can match by chance.
source: The barcode data indicate more inhibitory rather than excitatory neuron tangential migration, but the extent of migration is uncertain due to sparse sampling and because barcodes can match by chance.
evidence: The authors explicitly acknowledge this limitation in interpreting the migration data.

claim: The poor ability to detect localized excitatory neuron radial cortical migration with ~1000 cell whole brain trees may reflect that sparse sampling is unlikely to include multiple neurons from the same small clonal region.
source: The poor ability to detect localized excitatory neuron radial cortical migration with ~1000 cell whole brain trees (Figure 4C) may reflect that sparse sampling is unlikely to include multiple neurons from the same small clonal region that originated from common subventricular progenitors (radial unit hypothesis Rakic, 1988).
evidence: This is an inference based on the radial unit hypothesis and the observation that more localized migration is detected with more cells.

claim: Neurons of the same subtype were more related.
source: Neurons of the same subtype were still more related.
evidence: This is observed in the trees shown in Figure 4D and 4E where neurons cluster by subtype.

claim: Lineage trees appear to increase their resolution with more cells.
source: Hence, lineage trees appear to increase their resolution with more cells, albeit related lower and upper excitatory neuron pairs were still uncommon, which may reflect the unlikely chance of sampling very small radial clonal units.
evidence: This is an inference based on comparing trees with ~1000 cells versus ~2800 cells, showing improved detection of localized migration with more cells.

claim: Testing barcode performance is difficult because ideally samples obtained at different times would document how they change.
source: Dynamic barcodes would be useful to study human tissues, but testing their performance is difficult. Ideally, samples obtained at different times would document how they change.
evidence: This is a methodological consideration about the challenges of validating dynamic barcodes in human tissues.

claim: Specific neuron subsets recovered from the adult brain allow for sampling through time and before birth.
source: Specific neuron subsets recovered from the adult brain allow for sampling through time and before birth.
evidence: This is the key insight that enables barcode validation by using neurons that differentiated at different developmental times.

claim: The barcode appeared to start predominantly methylated in multiple individuals.
source: This serial sampling strategy facilitated fCpG barcode validation. The barcode appeared to start predominantly methylated in multiple individuals and became sufficiently polymorphic to distinguish between thousands of neurons.
evidence: This is based on the consistent pattern observed across all three brains showing high methylation in early-appearing neurons.

claim: Barcode changes appear to represent replication errors because they reconstruct lineage trees roughly consistent with caudal to rostral brain development.
source: Barcode changes appear to represent replication errors because they reconstruct lineage trees roughly consistent with caudal to rostral brain development.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observation that trees constructed from barcode data match expected developmental patterns.

claim: The current barcode is consistent with lineage dendrograms reconstructed with neuron-specific methylation of the same data.
source: The current barcode indicates that most inhibitory and excitatory neurons have relatively distinct progenitors, consistent with the lineage dendrograms reconstructed with neuron-specific methylation of the same data (Tian et al., 2023).
evidence: This comparison to previous analysis of the same dataset provides independent validation of the findings.

claim: Lineage trees indicate common progenitors for some inhibitory and excitatory neurons are present earlier in development.
source: Lineage trees indicate common progenitors are present earlier in development, and excitatory neurons that appear later do not have many closely related inhibitory neighbors (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is an inference based on the tree structure showing mixed inhibitory and excitatory neurons primarily in earlier branches.

claim: Hindbrain, excitatory, and non-neuronal cells had more subtype lineage fidelity.
source: Hindbrain, excitatory, and non-neuronal cells had more subtype lineage fidelity.
evidence: Figure 5B shows higher percentages of subtype fidelity for these cell types compared to inhibitory neurons.

claim: The approach remains speculative due to several factors: the absence of direct experimental validation, limited experimental cell sampling, and the possibility that barcode similarities may arise by chance rather than reflecting true biological relationships.
source: The approach remains speculative due to several factors: the absence of direct experimental validation, limited experimental cell sampling, and the possibility that barcode similarities may arise by chance rather than reflecting true biological relationships.
evidence: The authors explicitly acknowledge these limitations of the lineage fidelity analysis.

claim: Balanced fluctuating methylation is inferred in other tissues when CpG sites are ~50% methylated in bulk tissues.
source: Although average methylation decreases with time, both demethylation and remethylation are likely because fully demethylated neurons were not observed, and balanced fluctuating methylation is inferred in other tissues when CpG sites are ~50% methylated in bulk tissues (Gabbutt et al., 2022).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Gabbutt et al., 2022, describing the behavior of fCpGs in other tissues.

claim: Targeted bisulfite sequencing of a limited number of informative fCpGs could lead to more consistent coverage and less expensive sequencing of more neurons.
source: Technical improvements such as targeted bisulfite sequencing of a limited number of informative fCpGs could lead to more consistent coverage and less expensive sequencing of more neurons.
evidence: This is a speculative suggestion for future technical improvements.

claim: A common initialized state could facilitate standardized human fate maps and comparisons between individuals.
source: A common initialized state could facilitate standardized human fate maps and comparisons between individuals.
evidence: This is a speculative suggestion about potential applications if the methylated starting state is confirmed in more individuals.

claim: This preliminary survey indicates lineage heterogeneity between individuals.
source: Many polymorphisms linked to brain abnormalities such as autism are in neuronal proliferation, migration, and maturation pathways (Pan et al., 2019), and this preliminary survey indicates lineage heterogeneity between individuals (Figure 4A).
evidence: Figure 4A shows differences in tree structure between the three brains, particularly for H04.
